text:
clare: Quick sync  I'm planning a tiny docs PR that: clarifies SLA language for reserved pools vs autoscale, adds a concise eviction-priority table, and drops in 3 small codelets (YAML, HCL, Node). Aim: reduce support noise. Will open patch in ~1h. @omar @tess any must-have wording or examples?

omar: Please be explicit about "SLA-backed reserved pools" vs "best-effort autoscale". Ops keeps getting questions about uptime guarantees when teams only use autoscale. A one-sentence canonical blurb we can copy would be great.

clare: Draft blurb idea: "Reserved pools are SLA-backed for availability and latency targets. Reactive autoscale policies are best-effort to meet load spikes and are not covered by reserved-pool SLAs." OK to use?

omar: Perfect. Also include eviction precedence rules: numeric eviction_score examples and a short note on label precedence (tenant assignment > isolation label when a tenant is bound to a reserved pool).

tess: I can add small SDK snippets for Node + Python. Suggest we show a minimal createScalePolicy call and a note: "use labels to map workloads to reserved pools".

clare: Great. I'll add a tiny table like:

- eviction_score mapping: isolation=dedicated -> 0, tenant:reserved -> 5, isolation=shared -> 80
- precedence: tenant reserved assignment > isolation label > default pool

clare: YAML example for a steady policy (to include):

```yaml
scalePolicy:
  id: steady-75
  type: steady
  targets:
    cpu_utilization: 0.75
  labels:
    isolation: "dedicated"
    tenant: "analytics"
```

clare: HCL mapping (Terraform) suggestion:

```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_scale_policy" "steady" {
  pool_id = var.pool_id
  name    = "steady-75"
  policy = jsonencode({ type = "steady", targets = { cpu = 0.75 } })
  labels = { isolation = "dedicated" tenant = "analytics" }
}
```

tess: Node snippet coming up. Minimal and runnable is best. Also add note: prefer cooldown values as strings ("60s") in examples.

clare: Node quick snippet (will paste in PR):

```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.dedicated.createScalePolicy({
  poolId: 'pool-prod-01',
  name: 'steady-75',
  policy: { type: 'steady', targets: { cpu: 0.75 }, cooldown: '60s' },
  labels: { isolation: 'dedicated', tenant: 'analytics' }
});
```

omar: For the eviction table, can we add a runnable example mapping so readers can compute "effective eviction_score"? Something like:

- base by isolation: dedicated=10, shared=80
- tenant reserved override: tenant=5 if reserved
- final eviction_score = min(base, tenant_override)

omar: That usually helps reduce "which label wins" tickets.

clare: Nice. I'll add that algorithmic note + a short troubleshooting bullet: quota, warmup window, and label mismatch are the top three root causes when autoscale doesn't add instances.

docs-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4622 - docs: dedicated SLA + eviction examples + codelets. CI: lint OK, linkcheck: 1 warning (old TF anchor).

tess: I'll drop the Python snippet and a short explanation of how to set labels in the SDK in a follow-up commit.

clare: Thanks. @lucas can you confirm the anchor fix on provisioning page? docs-bot flagged it.

lucas: On it. I'll add the anchor `#terraform-reference` to the provisioning page and push. ETA 15m.

clare: Awesome. I'll wait for the anchor before merging. If CI and linkcheck are green after that I'll merge and backport the blurb into the reserved-pool FAQ page.

omar: :thumbsup: thanks for leading this.

clare: Tagging reviewers: @omar @tess @lucas. Merge after anchor + green CI. ETA today.
